claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the model for launch is policy-compliant on the basis of aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and a constrained 5% rollout with rollback capability, despite an unresolved Spanish-language billing support limitation.
specific_concerns: The available summary states the Spanish-language billing support segment remains below target and exposed in the initial cohort.
The policy text says rollout controls and monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
The summary states the risk acceptance draft is incomplete and not an approved acceptance covering the exposed risk.

The actor's compliance theory depends on explicit model-card disclosure of the limitation, but no admissible evidence is provided that such disclosure is actually completed and included in the certification packet.
Evidence access is limited to the actor's summary, so key predicates cannot be independently verified.
unsupported_claims: That the model can be certified now without further condition, when the required disclosure predicate is not evidenced.
That rollout controls alone materially cure the model-card weakness for the exposed Spanish-language billing use case.
That an incomplete risk acceptance draft provides policy coverage for the exposed limitation.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual approved model card or certification artifact showing explicit disclosure of the Spanish-language billing support limitation.
Provide evidence that the disclosed limitation is included in the launch decision record for the named use case.
Provide any reviewed and approved risk acceptance, if one exists, that specifically covers exposure of the Spanish-language billing segment in the initial rollout.
Provide the underlying policy excerpt or release checklist showing the exact disclosure requirement and how this launch satisfies it.
decision_criteria: A compliant certification requires admissible evidence that the materially limited named use case is either excluded from exposure or covered by approved risk acceptance, or that the required model-card disclosure is actually present in the certification record.
Aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one incidents, and rollback capability can support launch readiness but cannot substitute for the missing policy predicate.
Because the affected segment remains exposed and approved risk acceptance is absent, the certification case stands or falls on documented disclosure evidence.
